title: A fixed-stage splitting restricts to the actual normalization
statement: Let $B,A$ be commutative rings with $A$ a $B$-algebra such that $B\to A$ is ind-etale, meaning a filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $r,s\geq0$, $t:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to B$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, $p\in\mathbf N$, and $m>0$ coprime to $p$. Write $f=\prod_i t_i$, $C_m=B[x_i]/(x_i^m-t_i)$, $T_m=A[z_j]/(z_j^m-t_{\alpha(j)})$, $Q_m=T_m[1/f]$, $S_m=A\otimes_B C_m$, and $U_m=S_m[1/f]$, using the actual pushout presentations [def-sfb-active-root-normalization-pushout-data]. Assume the structural map $\iota:S_m\to U_m$ is injective and its image is exactly the elements integral over $S_m$. For any $B[1/f]$-algebra $D$, put $D_m=D\otimes_{B[1/f]}C_m[1/f]$ and $E_m=\operatorname{IntCl}_{C_m}(D_m)$. Let $d\geq0$ and let $\theta_m:D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_m\simeq Q_m^d$ be a specified $Q_m$-algebra isomorphism. There is a $B[1/f]$-algebra map $k:Q_m\to U_m$ sending $a\in A$ to $\iota(a\otimes1)$ and $z_j$ to $\iota(1\otimes x_{\alpha(j)})$. There is an $S_m$-algebra isomorphism $\Theta:D_m\otimes_{C_m}S_m\simeq U_m^d$ whose value on every $x\in D$ in coordinate $j$ is $k(\theta_m(x\otimes1)_j)$. There is an $S_m$-algebra isomorphism $\epsilon:E_m\otimes_{C_m}S_m\simeq S_m^d$ such that the actual closure inclusion followed by $\Theta$ equals $\epsilon$ followed by the coordinatewise structural localization $S_m^d\to U_m^d$. There is no infinite splitting, geometric-point, normality or finiteness hypothesis on $D$.

proof.text: Polynomial evaluation sending active roots to the corresponding full roots respects the monic equations. Its coefficient map is A -> S_m. Descend it to T_m -> S_m, and extend through the localization pushouts to k:Q_m -> U_m. These constructions give the stated equations on A and the root generators.

Extend the specified theta_m along k. Tensor pushout associativity identifies its source with D_m tensor_(C_m) S_m. Finite products commute with scalar extension by the coordinate idempotents, giving Theta with the specified equation on D.

Apply the same integral-closure base-change theorem a second time, now with $R=C_m$, ambient algebra $D_m$, integral closure $E_m$, and base algebra $S_m$. It gives the canonical identification $S_m\otimes_{C_m}E_m\simeq\operatorname{IntCl}_{S_m}(S_m\otimes_{C_m}D_m)$. The left hand side is $E_m\otimes_B A$ by tensor reassociation.

An algebra isomorphism preserves integrality: applying it, or its inverse, to a monic annihilating equation leaves its coefficients in the base ring. Therefore $\Theta$ identifies the closure in the base-change comparison with the integral closure of the diagonal $S_m$ in $S_m[1/f]^d$. If a tuple is integral, each coordinate is integral by applying its projection to the same monic equation; the assumed integral-closedness characterization puts every coordinate in $S_m$. Conversely a tuple $(s_1,\ldots,s_d)$ of elements of $S_m$ is annihilated by $\prod_{j=1}^d(X-s_j)$, evaluated diagonally: in coordinate $j$ its $j$-th factor vanishes. For $d=0$ the ambient ring is zero, the closure and $S_m^0$ are both zero, and the positive-degree monic polynomial $X$ annihilates its sole element. Thus this closure is exactly $S_m^d$. Restricting $\Theta$ now gives the asserted $S_m$-algebra isomorphism $E_m\otimes_B A\simeq S_m^d$.
